purpose: Document dated pre-1980 written Rarámuri forms containing -ami, -ame and -game in publicly catalogued titles, without imposing grammatical segmentation beyond the visible strings.

chronological_findings: A written Central form ending in -ami is catalogued by 1948, before Hilton 1959.
Western title forms ending in -game are catalogued by 1970 and recur in 1972, 1974 and 1975, before the 1978-1980 color-study fieldwork.
Western -ame forms are visible in titles by Albino Mares Trías in 1972 and 1974.

The pre-1980 written presence of these strings is therefore independent of the publication date of the 1983 color analysis, although several items belong to ILV/Burgess editorial or research networks.
epistemic_limits: Title strings alone do not establish morpheme boundaries, grammatical categories or glosses.
The 1948/1950 -ami form must not automatically be identified with participial -ame/-ami without contextual or grammatical confirmation.

The Western books are mediated by an ILV publishing environment; Burgess is author, investigator or associated researcher in several items, so institutional independence from his later scholarship is partial rather than complete.
Albino Mares Trías authors the 1972, 1974 and 1975 items, adding a community-authored usage layer, but editorial normalization may still be present.
research_value: These dated titles supply a documentary floor for the written circulation of -ami, -ame and -game strings before the late-1970s color experiments. They are especially useful as non-color usage controls once full text/context can be inspected.
next_steps: Retrieve page images or OCR for the 1972-1975 Mares Trías books and identify the contexts/glosses of the title forms.
Search the same texts for additional -game/-ame tokens and color vocabulary.
Inspect the 1948 and 1950 Central materials to determine the grammatical structure of osirúami rather than inferring it from the title alone.
